chunks: And in the narration of Abū al-Ḥusayn Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar al-Asadī, may Allah be pleased with him, from Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl al-Barmakī, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Aḥmad, from al-Faḍl ibn Ismāʿīl, from Muʿattib, the mawlā of al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام, who said: al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام said:

"Zakat was only instituted as a test for the wealthy and as assistance for the poor. If people were to pay the zakat of their wealth, no Muslim would remain poor and needy, and he would become free of need through what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has obligated for him.

People have not become impoverished, needy, hungry, or unclothed except because of the sins of the wealthy. And it is fitting upon Allah, Mighty and Majestic, to withhold His mercy from one who withholds the right of Allah in his wealth.

And I swear by the One who created creation and spread out sustenance: no wealth is lost on land or sea except through abandoning zakat, and no game is caught on land or sea except because of its abandoning glorification on that day.

Indeed, the most beloved of people to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, are those most generous in hand, and the most generous of people is the one who pays the zakat of his wealth and does not withhold from the believers what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has obligated for them in his wealth."

key_terms.اخْتِبَارًا: a test by which the wealthy are tried in obedience and generosity
key_terms.الرِّزْقَ: provision or sustenance distributed by Allah
key_terms.الزَّكَاةُ: the obligatory alms due on wealth as a divinely mandated financial duty
key_terms.الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: the believers who possess a rightful share in the wealth through Allah’s ordinance
key_terms.رَحْمَتَهُ: His mercy, which is withheld from one who denies Allah’s financial right
key_terms.لِلْفُقَرَاءِ: for the poor, meaning as support and relief for those in need

ai.seo_question: Why was zakat made obligatory, and how does neglecting it affect society?
ai.summary: This hadith explains that zakat was ordained both as a trial for the wealthy and as relief for the poor. It teaches that social deprivation results from the failure of the affluent to fulfill Allah’s right in their wealth, and it praises generosity and proper discharge of zakat as beloved to Allah.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.1579 - In a narration from Abu al-Husayn Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Asadi, may Allah (swt) be pleased with him, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Barmaki, from Abdullah ibn Ahmad, from al-Fadl ibn Isma'il, from Mu'attib, the servant of Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as):
Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) said:

"Zakat was ordained as a test for the wealthy and as support for the poor. If people paid the Zakat on their wealth, no Muslim would remain poor or in need. They would find sufficiency through what Allah (swt), the Almighty and Majestic, has prescribed for them.

People only become impoverished, needy, hungry, or unclothed because of the sins of the wealthy. It is a truth upon Allah (swt), the Almighty and Majestic, that He withholds His mercy from those who withhold Allah’s (swt) right in their wealth.

I swear by the One who created creation and spread sustenance that no wealth is lost on land or sea except due to the neglect of Zakat. And no prey is hunted on land or sea except due to the neglect of glorification (of Allah (swt)) on that day.

Indeed, the most beloved of people to Allah (swt), the Almighty and Majestic, are the most generous in giving, and the most generous of people is the one who pays the Zakat of his wealth and does not withhold from the believers what Allah (swt), the Almighty and Majestic, has ordained for them in his wealth."
